headline: High-risk shared-state orchestration plus unsandboxed server-side code creates dangerous write/conflict and cascading-error pathways; leakage and compliance risks are lower but real.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Langflow can ingest uploaded files and server-side flow outputs, while OpenBBTerminal exposes MCP/REST-style interfaces and a “connect once, consume everywhere” pattern. That creates a plausible bridge where attacker-controlled content from one side can be treated as instructions by the other. The pathway is not proven by docs alone, so I choose medium over low.
conditions: IF Langflow flow outputs are copied into OpenBBTerminal prompts or MCP inputs
IF either side treats file or API content as trusted instructions
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of upstream text as instructions
Add explicit provenance labels to all inter-agent payloads
Require human review before executing tool calls from imported content
Use a fixed schema for exchanged messages
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance enforcement

B_data_leakage.rationale: Langflow touches flow inputs, intermediate outputs, and uploaded files on the server filesystem; OpenBBTerminal touches financial, licensed, and public data and exposes FastAPI/MCP/REST interfaces. If the pair shares a workspace or passes files between them, sensitive financial or licensed data can leak into Langflow outputs or logs. The shared-workspace path is plausible but not confirmed, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF the two agents share a filesystem, volume, or copied artifacts
IF OpenBBTerminal data is routed through Langflow prompts, logs, or stored flow outputs
mitigations: Separate workspaces and credentials per agent
Avoid passing raw financial files through Langflow
Redact licensed or sensitive fields before transfer
Turn off verbose logging for shared runs
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Langflow has broad filesystem write, shell, subprocess, and broad network egress; OpenBBTerminal exposes MCP/REST/FastAPI interfaces and supports multiple instances. If both operate on the same mutable workspace or shared server-side state, concurrent writes and conflicting tool actions can corrupt state or overwrite outputs. Because Langflow’s shared state is explicit and OpenBBTerminal can be driven through APIs, the conflict is dangerous by default in shared deployments.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory, database, or server-side store
IF OpenBBTerminal API actions and Langflow flow writes run concurrently without locks
mitigations: Assign separate writable directories
Serialize writes with a lock or queue
Disable concurrent runs against shared state
Snapshot state before each run
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: Langflow can chain multiple agents and run unsandboxed Python code server-side, so its outputs may be treated as authoritative workflow inputs. OpenBBTerminal exposes APIs that can act on those inputs, and its “connect once, consume everywhere” pattern increases the chance of downstream reuse without verification. That makes a bad Langflow output capable of cascading into incorrect financial actions or reports.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal consumes Langflow-generated facts without independent validation
IF Langflow code components or agents emit incorrect market or portfolio data
mitigations: Require validation before any downstream action
Mark Langflow outputs as untrusted by default
Add checksum or schema checks between agents
Limit OpenBBTerminal to read-only mode for chained runs
requires-engineering: implement verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: Langflow stores per-flow credentials and handles flow inputs/intermediate outputs, while OpenBBTerminal touches financial and licensed data. If regulated financial or licensed data is routed through Langflow’s server-side store or logs, retention and residency obligations may diverge from OpenBBTerminal’s handling. The profiles do not show a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated financial or licensed data is stored in Langflow flow state or logs
IF retention or deletion requests must be honored across both systems
mitigations: Minimize retention in Langflow stores
Avoid placing regulated data in flow variables
Document a shared deletion workflow
Review logging settings before production use
requires-engineering: align residency and retention policies
